coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay Preliminary Utilities Plant
record.summary: A utility plant on Block 16B that a 2017 CEQA notice of determination (received August 4, 2017) calls the 'existing Preliminary Utility Plant (PUP)'; the notice concerns new utility lines to the planned Weill Neurosciences Building and does not say the plant is central or which buildings it serves. Construction date, architect and size were not found in any source checked.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap outline of the plant's fenced compound (OSM way 135103720 is tagged landuse=industrial with a fence barrier, not as a building), not a hand trace or plan estimate; the polygon is the fenced site, not a building footprint. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data and tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

open_questions: Searched again on 2026-09-21 for a dated construction record specifically for this plant (Block 16B), including UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings agenda items. Item 101C of May 17, 2000, for the Mission Bay Developmental Biology and Genetics Building (19B) (p. 2), says that building would have 'a stand-alone utility plant, due to the lack of central facility support during Phase 1 development at Mission Bay' -- a plant for that building, not shown to be this one. The only CEQA document read, a Notice of Determination for the UCSF Mission Bay Utility Distribution System Extension (SCH 2013092047; approved July 31, 2017, received August 4, 2017), refers to 'the existing Preliminary Utility Plant (PUP) on Block 16B' and a 'planned Weill Neurosciences Building'; this confirms 'PUP' as the plant's abbreviation and that it existed by July 2017, but gives no construction date of its own. An earlier version of this note described a 2021 CEQA addendum; none was read, and the wording comes from the 2017 notice. Still no dated milestone found; none added rather than guessed.
No construction date, architect, or engineer found in any source checked -- deliberately left undated rather than guessed.

Street address: the OpenStreetMap tag is 1480 4th St; the cited CEQA filing gives Block 16B but no street address. An earlier version of this record said a CEQA filing gave 1500 Owens St; no record read states that, so it was removed on 2026-09-29 (a 1500 Owens St address exists as a UCSF Health radiology clinic, which is a different use). No street address for the plant is confirmed beyond the OpenStreetMap tag.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be read); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further as of 2026-09-21; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history.
No source gives a completion date. DBI's permit dataset has no new-construction permit at 1480 4th St, and the Assessor roll has no year built for the plant.

OpenStreetMap maps the plant (way 135103720) as a fenced industrial site (tags landuse=industrial and barrier=fence), not as a building, so the outline shown is the compound, not a building footprint.

Role of the utility plant: the 2017 CEQA notice describes extending mechanical utility lines from connections south of Rock Hall to Byers Hall and the planned Weill Neurosciences Building; the notice does not say the plant is 'central' or which buildings it serves overall.
